title: Interactive Arithmetic Logic: GCD, LCM & Euclidean Modulo
mechanisms_and_formulas: Euclidean algorithm: while B ≠ 0, R = A % B; A = B; B = R; result = A
Time complexity of Euclidean algorithm: O(log(min(A,B)))
examples_and_code_patterns: Example: A=12, B=18 → first iteration 12 % 18 = 12, resulting in A=18, B=12 (implicit swap)
Overflow‑safe LCM computation: compute (A / GCD) * B instead of (A * B) / GCD
factual_summary_text: The material explains how to compute the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of two integers using the relationship LCM(A,B) * GCD(A,B) = A * B, which simplifies to LCM = (A * B) / GCD. It then introduces the Euclidean algorithm as an efficient method for finding the Greatest Common Divisor (GCD), avoiding repeated subtraction. The algorithm repeatedly replaces the pair (A,B) with (B, A % B) until B becomes zero, at which point A holds the GCD. This process runs in logarithmic time, O(log(min(A,B))). An example shows that when A < B (e.g., A=12, B=18), the first modulo operation naturally swaps the values without an explicit swap. Finally, the content warns about integer overflow when calculating (A * B) / GCD and recommends performing the division first as (A / GCD) * B, especially in languages like C++ or Java.
